newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric welcomes DTI decision.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric welcomes DTI decision.

text.p: Northern Electric Plc said on Friday that it welcomed the UK's decision not to refer the hostile takeover bid from U.S. utility CE Electric.
The British government announced earlier today that it had cleared the 782 million stg bid for Northern Electric.
The clearance comes just ahead of next Friday's closure of the 650 pence-per-share offer for Northern.

David Morris, chairman of Northern Electric, said, "CE Electric chose to declare its offer final before the release of our key information. It now finds itself in the uncomfortable position of trying to persuade our shareholders to give up almost one stg per share in dividends over the next nine months and to forego a prospective 1997/8 yield of over 10.5 percent in return for a price which clearly short changes them."
Northern Electric also said that institutional shareholder Prudential has bought further shares at over 600p per share.

CE Electric welcomed the UK's decision not to refer its bid. It said in a statement "The decision for shareholders is now crystal clear. In contrast to Northern Electric's board's suggestion that shareholders should forgo cash for their shares and instead wait to see what an uncertain future holds, CE Electric's final offer... is real and certain today."
